ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, the left side is a fixed wall, and the left end of the rope is fixed at point O on the wall; the rope extends horizontally to the right from point O to the fixed smooth axle or pulley near point O′, and the segment OO′ is a horizontal segment; a light ring is sleeved on the horizontal rope segment; after the rope goes around the smooth axle at O′ on the right side, it goes vertically downward, and an object of mass M is suspended at the end. Then reason: let the mass of the hook weight hung on the light ring be m, and after equilibrium the position of the light ring be A. The problem gives OO′=L, and the object M rises by L. Since the rope is inextensible, the vertical suspended segment on the right side shortens by L, so the original horizontal segment OO′ of length L becomes the broken line OA+AO′ after the light ring is pulled downward, and this broken line is longer than the original horizontal segment by L; therefore OA+AO′=L+L=2L. The rope, pulley, and light ring are all smooth, so the tension is the same everywhere in the same light rope. The object of mass M at the right end is in equilibrium, so the tension in the rope is T=Mg. The light ring is acted on by the equal tensions T of the two rope segments on the left and right and the gravity mg of the hook weight. Since the gravity of the hook weight is vertically downward, when the light ring is in equilibrium, the horizontal components of the tensions on the two sides must cancel each other, so A is on the perpendicular bisector of OO′, and hence OA=AO′. Also OA+AO′=2L, so OA=AO′=L. Combined with OO′=L, triangle OAO′ is an equilateral triangle, and the angle between each rope segment and the horizontal is 60°. Write the equilibrium equation in the vertical direction for the light ring: 2T sin60°=mg. Substituting T=Mg gives mg=2Mg·sin60°=√3 Mg, therefore m=√3M.

raw_record.question_text: As shown in the figure, an inextensible smooth light rope has its left end fixed at point O, and its right end passes over a fixed smooth axle located at point O′ and suspends an object of mass M; the segment OO′ is horizontal, with length L; a light ring that can slide along the rope is sleeved on the rope. Now a hook weight is hung on the light ring, and after equilibrium, the object rises by L. Then what is the mass of the hook weight?

method.method_draft: 先从图中确认：左端 O 固定在墙上，右侧 O′ 是定滑轮，OO′ 为水平段，原来轻环套在这段绳上，右侧竖直绳端挂质量 M。设挂在轻环上的钩码质量为 m，平衡时轻环位置为 A。由题文读出 OO′=L，物体 M 上升 L，绳不可伸长、光滑。物体 M 上升 L 表示右侧竖直绳段缩短 L，因此 O 到 A 再到 O′ 的折线绳长比原水平 OO′ 段增加 L，即 OA+AO′=2L。由于绳和滑轮、轻环均光滑，同一根绳张力处处相等，且右端挂物 M 平衡，所以张力 T=Mg。轻环处受两侧等大张力和钩码重力，水平分力必须抵消，因此 A 在 OO′ 的中垂线上，OA=AO′=L。结合 OO′=L，三角形 OAO′ 为边长 L、L、L 的等边三角形，或每段绳与水平夹角为 60°。轻环竖直方向平衡：2T sin60°=mg，代入 T=Mg，得 m=√3 M。
method.CoT_raw:
先描述图像：图中左侧是固定墙壁，绳的左端固定在墙上 O 点；绳从 O 点水平向右延伸到 O′ 点附近的固定光滑轴或滑轮处，OO′ 段为水平段；水平绳段上套有一个轻环；绳绕过右侧 O′ 处的光滑轴后竖直向下，末端悬挂质量为 M 的物体。

再推理：设轻环上悬挂的钩码质量为 m，平衡后轻环位置为 A。题给 OO′=L，物体 M 上升 L。由于绳不可伸长，右侧竖直悬挂段缩短 L，所以原来水平段 OO′ 的长度 L 在轻环下拉后变成折线 OA+AO′，并且该折线比原水平段增加 L，因此 OA+AO′=L+L=2L。

绳、滑轮和轻环均光滑，同一根轻绳张力处处相等。右端质量 M 的物体平衡，所以绳中张力 T=Mg。

轻环受左右两段绳的等大张力 T 以及钩码重力 mg。由于钩码重力竖直向下，轻环平衡时两侧张力的水平分力必须相互抵消，所以 A 在 OO′ 的中垂线上，于是 OA=AO′。又 OA+AO′=2L，所以 OA=AO′=L。结合 OO′=L，三角形 OAO′ 为等边三角形，每段绳与水平夹角为 60°。

对轻环竖直方向列平衡方程：2T sin60°=mg。代入 T=Mg，得 mg=2Mg·sin60°=√3 Mg，因此 m=√3M。

raw_record.original_question: 如图所示，一不可伸长的光滑轻绳，左端固定于 O 点，右端跨过位于 O′ 点的固定光滑轴悬挂一质量为 M 的物体；OO′ 段水平，长度为 L；绳子上套一可沿绳滑动的轻环。现在轻环上悬挂一钩码，平衡后，物体上升 L。则钩码的质量是多少？
raw_record.final_cot:
First describe the image: in the figure, the left side is a fixed wall, and the left end of the rope is fixed at point O on the wall; the rope extends horizontally to the right from point O to the fixed smooth axle or pulley near point O′, and the segment OO′ is a horizontal segment; a light ring is sleeved on the horizontal rope segment; after the rope goes around the smooth axle at O′ on the right side, it goes vertically downward, and an object of mass M is suspended at the end.

Then reason: let the mass of the hook weight hung on the light ring be m, and after equilibrium the position of the light ring be A. The problem gives OO′=L, and the object M rises by L. Since the rope is inextensible, the vertical suspended segment on the right side shortens by L, so the original horizontal segment OO′ of length L becomes the broken line OA+AO′ after the light ring is pulled downward, and this broken line is longer than the original horizontal segment by L; therefore OA+AO′=L+L=2L.

The rope, pulley, and light ring are all smooth, so the tension is the same everywhere in the same light rope. The object of mass M at the right end is in equilibrium, so the tension in the rope is T=Mg.

The light ring is acted on by the equal tensions T of the two rope segments on the left and right and the gravity mg of the hook weight. Since the gravity of the hook weight is vertically downward, when the light ring is in equilibrium, the horizontal components of the tensions on the two sides must cancel each other, so A is on the perpendicular bisector of OO′, and hence OA=AO′. Also OA+AO′=2L, so OA=AO′=L. Combined with OO′=L, triangle OAO′ is an equilateral triangle, and the angle between each rope segment and the horizontal is 60°.

Write the equilibrium equation in the vertical direction for the light ring: 2T sin60°=mg. Substituting T=Mg gives mg=2Mg·sin60°=√3 Mg, therefore m=√3M.
